result.reason: The passage directly quotes the mishna's opening case of the boat not entering port and Rabban Gamliel's resolution, which is precisely what the 'Setup & Rabban Gamliel' prose describes.

The passage describes the baraita about Rabban Gamliel's tube (shfoferet) and its use for measuring distances on land and sea, which is precisely what the 'Shfoferet Device' section's prose discusses.
Both items describe measuring a valley's depth and a palm tree's height using the shfoferet/proportional methods, which is exactly what candidate 2 ('Valley & Tree Measuring') discusses in its prose.

The passage describes the grave shadow remedy using a reed to prevent wild beasts from resting in the shade of a grave, which directly matches the prose in candidate 0 about inserting a stick to observe shadows and deter dangerous creatures from congregating at a tombstone.

Both items describe the narrative of Nechemya getting lost outside the techum and the immediate solution proposed — exactly what candidate 0 ('Nechemya's Story') introduces, while the current placement (candidate 1) actually discusses the solution's halakhic implications which come after the narrative itself.

The passage depicts Rav Naḥman bar Yitzḥak asking Rava what exactly Rav Ḥisda's dilemma was, which directly matches the 'Question on Solution' prose describing this very exchange and question about what difficulty prompted Rav Ḥisda to seek guidance.

All four items form a continuous gemara discussion resolving whether the case involved sufficient people (bi-demalu) or insufficient people (bi-de-lo malu), concluding it must be the latter and that the dilemma was about Rabbi Eliezer's ruling — exactly the content described in the 'Two Cubit Problem' prose, including the peshita resolution and the precision from 'yikanes'.

The passage is the first baraita prohibition against making temporary partitions/tents on Shabbat, which matches exactly the 'First Braita Prohibition' prose describing this challenge to using people as walls.

The passage is Rava's citation of the second baraita permitting a person as a wall and upturning a bed to shade a corpse, which is exactly what heading 0 ('Second Braita Permission') describes in its prose.

Both items are the core content of the 'Reconciliation Attempt' section: item 1 is the Rabbi Eliezer/Rabbanan resolution via the window shutter mishna, and item 2 is Rabba bar bar Ḥana's statement in the name of Rabbi Yoḥanan that rejects that resolution — exactly what the prose of candidate 0 describes.
All five items deal with the Rabbi Meir/Rabbi Yehuda animal-wall debate and its dismantling, which is precisely what the 'Animal Wall Debate' prose describes in detail.

All three items form the gemara's resolution distinguishing the third from fourth wall, which is precisely what candidate 0 ('Third vs. Fourth Wall') describes in its prose, including the *nafal dofenah* linguistic proof cited in item 3.

The passage raises the unresolved contradiction between two rulings about using a person as a sukkah wall, which is a tension about what constitutes a valid halachic wall — most directly relevant to the 'Halachic Wall Defined' section's discussion of constitutive wall-making, though the fit is imperfect since the prose there focuses on the third-wall distinction rather than the person-as-wall issue.

The passage directly resolves the contradiction about a person serving as a wall through the knowing/unknowing distinction (la-da'at / she-lo mi-da'at), which is precisely what the 'Unaware People Rule' prose section discusses.

This passage illustrates the da'at/she-lo mi-da'at distinction with a specific case (Rabbi Neḥemya son of Rabbi Ḥanilai), which fits under 'Unaware Examples' where the gemara's illustrative cases are discussed, rather than under 'Unaware People Rule' which covers the theoretical principle itself.

All four items discuss the same topic of human partitions used knowingly vs. unknowingly on Shabbat — the Rav Ḥisda clarification, Shmuel's flogging of the wedding party, Rava's flask cases, and the examples of Levi/Ze'eiri/Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya — all of which are explicitly summarized in the 'Unaware Examples' prose.

The mishna text directly describes the case where someone went out with permission and was told the action was already performed, receiving two thousand amot from their current location — exactly what the 'Services Unneeded' section's prose discusses.

The passage directly states the mishna's ruling about being within the original techum and the principle that those who go out to save lives may return to their original locations, which is precisely what the 'Original Techum Reversion' prose discusses.

All three items together constitute the Gemara's discussion of the mishna's phrase 'as if he never left,' with Rabba's interpretation (items 1-2) and Rav Shimi bar Ḥiyya's interpretation (item 3) — the latter being exactly the 'overlapping techumim' reading that candidate 0's prose describes.
The passage explicitly states the core dispute about whether havla'at techumim 'is something' significant or not, which is precisely what the 'Overlap Debate' section's prose discusses.

Both items are the Abaye-Rabba exchange about the cave case (havla'at techumim) and Rabba's distinction regarding establishing residence within mechitzot from before Shabbat, which is precisely what the 'Cave Example' prose describes.
